items.rationale: In an agent the model owns the control flow: it picks the next action or stops. A fixed list of steps written in advance describes a workflow.
The agent makes 5 - 2 = 3 extra calls per request, and 3 x 200 = 600. An answer of 400 or 1000 counts only one of the two designs.
When the steps and their order are known and never change, a fixed workflow is cheaper, more predictable and easier to test than an agent.
The program decides which step runs next, so it is a workflow; a model call inside it, even one that picks a branch, does not hand over the control flow.
When the path cannot be written in advance because each finding decides the next check, the model must own the control flow, so an agent fits.
A step that must always happen belongs in code, because a model may skip or reorder it; this is the reliability reason to use a fixed workflow.
